issues.issue: The paragraph makes the Agreement void unless employment commences by the March 19, 2013 initial start date, yet makes the Agreement effective only when all parties have signed (here the employee signed 3/21/2013). Whether the condition precedent or the later Effective Date controls is an internal ambiguity in these very words.

"Complete satisfactorily all assignments and training obligations" fixes no standard, and the materials and assistance owed are only what Wells Fargo "in its sole discretion deems reasonable and necessary." Both terms leave the employee's and employer's duties without a measurable boundary.

"At least initially, you will be eligible for overtime pay" sets no end point for overtime eligibility, and the starting salary figure is never stated in the Agreement. The duration of overtime eligibility is left to be construed from words that fix nothing.

This paragraph ends overtime eligibility on the title change, while Paragraph 3 promises overtime eligibility "at least initially" and pays salary bi-weekly, so the two must be read together to know when overtime stops. It also routes post-graduation "monthly compensation and a monthly draw" through the "New FA Compensation Plan" that Paragraph 3 defines as the plan for New FA employees.

Failing the Series 7 midterm or the licensing exams "may lead to consequences, up to and including termination from the Training Program" — "consequences" is undefined and discretionary. Nothing in the paragraph bounds what else may follow a failure.

The closing sentence preserves all Wells Fargo human resources policies, programs and compliance guidelines as binding alongside this document, which cannot be squared with Paragraph 20's statement that the Agreement is the entire understanding regarding the matters addressed. Which body of terms governs a subject covered by both must be construed.

The declaration that the employee is "not hired for any specified term or duration pursuant to a contract of employment" and may be terminated at any time sits against Paragraph 10(b)(i), which conditions forgiveness of Training Costs on five years of continuous employment, and Paragraph 10(a), which imposes repayment on termination for any reason. Whether at-will status is compatible with a five-year financial tether is a relational question.

The statement that "[t]his Agreement serves only as a synopsis of the compensation and other arrangements" casts doubt on whether the document is itself binding or only a summary of terms residing elsewhere. "Synopsis" is the ambiguous word, and it is the same word the modification sentence then treats as the thing being amended.

The carve-out letting Wells Fargo modify, amend or terminate any compensation or benefit plan or policy in its sole discretion cannot be squared with Paragraph 20's entire-understanding clause or with the Paragraph 3 promise that compensation is paid in accordance with the New FA Compensation Plan. Which document supplies the operative compensation terms is left open.

"Any revenue or fees 'fronted' or advanced ... together with any other awards or advanced compensation" and "deficit balances (unrelated to the offset of the draw)" are undefined and set no boundary on what may be clawed back. The catch-all "any other awards or advanced compensation" sits loosely against the enumerated fronted revenue and fees.

This subparagraph denies any interest in revenue or fees unless the employee is employed on the payout date, while Paragraph 9(a) makes Wells Fargo liable for "compensation earned and received by Wells Fargo Advisors" before the termination date. The two cannot both govern revenue that Wells Fargo received before termination but pays after it.

The two dollar amounts of Training Costs that the paragraph says are "set forth below" are blank in the executed document, so the sum the employee agreed to repay is not stated. The obligation to "reimburse Wells Fargo Advisors for these Training Costs" has no ascertainable amount within its own terms.

The five-year forgiveness period here runs from the later of graduation and full registration, whereas Paragraph 10(c) amortizes the same Training Costs by 1/48 per month from the second year of employment as a New FA, extinguishing the debt on a different date. The two exit routes from the same obligation cannot both be given effect.

"Competitive Organization or Entity" is defined "as including, but not be limited to" a list of financial firms plus "any other person, firm, corporation, or entity that competes with Wells Fargo Advisors" — a catch-all with no ascertainable limit given Wells Fargo's breadth of businesses. Whether the general words are confined to the enumerated kinds is exactly the ejusdem generis question.

The 1/48-per-month amortization beginning in the second year of New FA employment retires the Training Costs on a schedule measured from hire, while Paragraph 10(b)(i) measures the five-year forgiveness period from graduation and full registration. The amount owed on a given termination date differs depending on which provision is applied.

Setoff is taken "in the calculation of your monthly compensation," but Paragraph 3 pays a New FA a bi-weekly salary with overtime and Paragraph 4 makes monthly compensation available only after the title change. The mechanism has no subject matter for the very population Paragraph 10 addresses.

Item (ii) sweeps in "[a]ll records and other documents made and/or maintained in connection with Wells Fargo Advisors business" without regard to confidentiality, far outrunning the trade-secret and client-information categories enumerated in item (i). Whether the general category is limited to genuinely confidential material is the construction question.

The surrender obligation is imposed on "any Confidential Records or Documents," a term never defined, whereas Paragraph 11(a) defines "Confidential Information and Documents." Whether the surrender duty reaches the defined category or something narrower turns on this mismatch of terms.

The bar covers any client the employee "had contact with or otherwise learned of during the course of your employment," and "otherwise learned of" has no ascertainable boundary. Whether it reaches clients merely seen on a firm list is the term needing construction.

The one-year period runs from "your termination of employment by Wells Fargo Advisors," which can be read as covering only employer-initiated terminations, unlike Paragraph 12(a), which expressly reaches voluntary resignation. Whether a resigning employee is bound at all depends on that phrase.

The employee "will be expected to contribute" an amount "determined after a consultation" with management — neither the obligation nor the amount is fixed, and it is unclear whether this creates a binding duty or an expectation. There is no formula or cap for the contribution.

"You are subject to disciplinary action for trading errors that may have a financial impact on future earnings" leaves the modifier floating: it is unclear whether the errors or the discipline is what affects future earnings. The sentence's grammar changes who bears the loss.

"Net Eligible Revenue" is capitalized as a defined term but is nowhere defined in the Agreement, existing only in the extrinsic New FA Compensation Plan. The size of any adjustment therefore cannot be determined from the instrument's own words.
